mission_context: ExoMars Rosalind Franklin Rover Landing Site (ESA/Roscosmos/NASA)
scientific_summary: Exposes an ancient (~4.0 Ga, Noachian) stratiform clay sheet spanning thousands of square kilometers. Unlike volatile lake deposits that underwent acidic desiccation, Oxia Planum represents a persistent, neutral-pH, habitable water-rock alteration epoch subsequently preserved by cryogenic freeze-drying and gentle aeolian deflation.
geological_epoch: Circa 4.0 Ga (Noachian to Early Hesperian boundary)

coordinates.datum: MOLA areoid (0 m elevation defined at mean radius 3396.0 km)

elevation.name: surface_elevation
elevation.citation: Fergason et al. (2018), Quantin-Nataf et al. (2021)

slope.name: regional_slope
slope.notes: 98% of landing ellipse area has slopes < 5 degrees

surface_roughness_rms.name: decameter_rms_roughness
surface_roughness_rms.instrument: MGS MOLA 1-km baseline pulse width / HiRISE
surface_roughness_rms.notes: Relatively smooth, low-relief plain with isolated resistant remnant buttes

temperature_mean_annual.name: surface_temperature_annual_mean
temperature_mean_annual.instrument: Mars Climate Database (MCD v6.1) / MGS TES
temperature_mean_annual.citation: Forget et al. (1999), Millour et al. (2018)
temperature_mean_annual.notes: Equivalent to -60.65 deg C annual mean surface temperature

temperature_diurnal_range.name: diurnal_temperature_amplitude
temperature_diurnal_range.notes: Severe diurnal swing typical of thin Martian atmosphere and low thermal inertia

thermal_inertia.citation: Edwards et al. (2011), Fergason et al. (2018)
thermal_inertia.notes: Corresponds to cohesive duricrust / moderately indurated clay-bearing regolith

albedo_bolometric.name: bolometric_visible_albedo
albedo_bolometric.notes: Intermediate albedo, indicating exposed bedrock with thin, non-continuous dust

dust_cover_index.name: dust_cover_index_dci
dust_cover_index.notes: DCI > 0.95 indicates a dust-poor, rock/duricrust-dominated surface

clay_phyllosilicate_index.citation: Carter et al. (2015), Quantin-Nataf et al. (2021)

water_equivalent_hydrogen.instrument: Mars Odyssey GRS / HEND Neutron Spectrometer
water_equivalent_hydrogen.citation: Boynton et al. (2007), Feldman et al. (2004)
water_equivalent_hydrogen.notes: Water bound in clay mineral lattice (structural OH/H2O); zero liquid water

atmospheric_pressure.name: mean_surface_pressure
atmospheric_pressure.instrument: MCD v6.1 scaled to MOLA elevation -3050 m

irreducible_limits.surface_gravity: Mars = 3.71 m/s^2 (0.38g) vs Earth = 9.81 m/s^2 (1.00g). Affects saltation threshold and rover chassis dynamics.
irreducible_limits.atmospheric_pressure: Mars = ~7.55 hPa (0.0075 atm) pure CO2 vs Earth = 1013 hPa N2/O2. Sublimation kinetics and aerodynamic rotorcraft testing diverge.
irreducible_limits.radiation_environment: Oxia Planum has zero magnetic shielding and negligible atmosphere; annual cosmic ray/SPE surface dose is ~230 mSv/yr.
irreducible_limits.biological_sterility: Oxia Planum is an abiotic, hyper-arid surface exposed to UV-C; Earth analogs contain active microbial extremophiles.

recommended_earth_analog_archetypes: Cold-desert clay playas (e.g. McMurdo Dry Valleys paleolake sediments)
Hyper-arid high-altitude evaporite basins (Tibetan Qaidam Basin, Puna-Altiplano salars)
Wind-deflated smectite clay massifs (Western Desert of Egypt)
